title: Goal
description: A canonical goal, at <venture>/foundation/goals/<id>.json: what the venture means to reach, by when, how anyone would know (measures with targets) and who owns it. Framework-neutral: the telos, ambition tiers, OKRs and other frameworks for thinking write goals through their maps_to and never change this shape (Torian, 2026-10-30: opinionated schema, swappable frameworks). Requirements derive from goals and measures; exit criteria serve measures. A goal is a durable record, like the decision ledger (EE-210): it carries a status only a person settles, the goal it serves, the goals it replaces, and every version of it stays readable from the provenance log and the blob store (naive goals history, packages/naive/src/store/as-of.ts).

kind.description: venture: the end the venture exists for. owner: what the owners intend once it is reached (hold, sell, list, wind down). scale: how far through the phases the venture means to go. product, function: a goal of one product or function. learning: what the venture must find out

status.description: Where the goal stands (EE-210). A record with no status is proposed, so goals written before the ledger stay valid. Only a person moves a goal on (naive goals status <id> <status> --by <person>); an agent proposes one, and its write of a lifecycle field is held as a draft whatever the gate says, as a write that settles a decision is (EE-058). The transitions, in packages/naive/src/engine/goals.ts LIFECYCLE: proposed to active, dropped or superseded; active to met, missed, dropped or superseded; a settled goal reopens only to active. A goal nobody adopted is never met or missed.

status_by.description: The person who set the current status. Never an agent

status_at.description: When the current status was set

due.description: The date by which the goal should be met or missed, when it has one. horizon is the ambition (a year, a phase or open); due is the date the ledger measures against

parent.description: The goal this one serves, by id: a function or product goal serves a venture goal. A goal with no parent is a root, and no parent chain may cycle (packages/naive/src/checks/check-goals.ts)

supersedes.description: The goals this one replaces, by id. A person records the replacement on both sides: the old goal's status becomes superseded and its superseded_by names this one

superseded_by.description: The goal that replaced this one, by id. Set exactly when the status is superseded

horizon.description: The year it should be reached by, a date, a phase id, or 'open'

end_state.description: What is true in the world when it is reached

value.description: A goal's chosen value when its kind has a fixed set: the scale (hobby, survival, lifestyle, managed-growth, aggressive-growth) or the owner path (acquisition, ipo, secondary-sale, merger, management-buyout, wind-down, hold)

kind.description: A framework's own classification of the measure, kept as written

result.description: What happened, written when a person settles the goal as met or missed. It carries a note, or each measure as it stood, or both; check-goals.ts fails a met or missed goal with neither

note.description: What happened, in the person's words

measures.description: Each measure of this goal as it stood when the goal was settled

id.description: A measure id of this goal

evidence.description: Evidence ids or venture-relative paths behind the value

owner.description: The person or role who owns the goal

sources.description: Where the goal came from, so a reader of the goal alone can trace it: a venture-relative path (raw/sources/<id>.json, raw/dump.mdx), a raw source id, or a record ref such as decisions/<id>. Not checked against the files

framework.description: The framework for thinking the goal was written through (frameworks/<id>), if any

conversation.description: The founder's messages this record was made from (naive diagnose catches)
